body:
**Action.** At engine start, register the platform's fonts with EffectCraft through `effectcraft_text::add_source(&DirectorySource { dirs })` (AD2). On iOS, `dirs` is the set of parent folders of the font files CoreText reports (`CTFontCollectionCreateFromAvailableFonts` with `kCTFontURLAttribute`), never a hard-coded `/System/Library/Fonts`: in the simulator that is the Mac's folder, and iOS keeps PingFang in `PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/CorePrivate` (V1). On Android, `/system/fonts`. Add the app's `Folders.fonts`. Bundle Noto Sans SC Regular and Noto Sans TC Regular, noto-cjk's region-subset OTFs (`Sans/SubsetOTF/SC/NotoSansSC-Regular.otf`, `Sans/SubsetOTF/TC/NotoSansTC-Regular.otf`, 14.0 MB together, SIL OFL 1.1, its LICENSE shipped with them and both listed in ATTRIBUTION.md), because iOS 26's PingFang has only `hvgl` outlines that EffectCraft cannot draw, and both family names are on EffectCraft's Chinese fallback lists. Every face in those folders stays registered, so drawing and fallback keep all of them. The font list is filtered in `craftbridge-effects`, never in EffectCraft: on iOS, keep a registered face only when its (file, PostScript name) pair, `FaceData::File` and `FaceInfo.postscript`, is one of CoreText's descriptors (`kCTFontURLAttribute`, `kCTFontNameAttribute`), and list the families of the kept faces plus the bundled families. That filter answers every path a CraftBridge app reaches the list by: the `list_fonts` method, `exec` of `text.fonts`, the `mcp` line `list_fonts`, and a script's `executeCommand("text.fonts")`. Each answer has the command's own shape, with `count` recomputed. Where the platform supplies no face list (Android, the desktop conformance runs), the list passes through unfiltered, so the conformance corpus still compares like with like (§28). AD2's entry in `tools/adaptations.toml` also lists `text.fonts` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text_edit.rs`) and `effectcraft_text::families`, which the filter relies on. Why: the owner chose a font list that matches iOS's own exactly, with nothing lost from drawing. V1 measured that face matching gives exactly the 86 `UIFont.familyNames` on the simulator and the iPhone (266 of 633 faces). Registering only those faces would leave 134 script families, among them the Noto fonts for Adlam, Cuneiform and Egyptian Hieroglyphs, with no covering face; filtering the listing keeps them all drawable.

**Acceptance.** On the simulator, every path above lists exactly `UIFont.familyNames` (81 by English name, Al Nile, Damascus, Farah, Geeza Pro and Mishafi under their Arabic names) plus the bundled families, with a matching `count`, while all registered faces still draw: a character of a script only an unlisted face covers (for example Adlam 𞤀) falls back to that face, not to a missing-glyph box. The bundled files report the families `Noto Sans SC` and `Noto Sans TC`; 汉 (zh-Hans) falls back to Noto Sans SC/Regular and 漢 (zh-Hant) to Noto Sans TC/Regular. On the emulator, `list_fonts` shows the system families.

**Plan.** §19, R3, AD2, V1 · wave W2 · team FX · 1.5 engineer-days

Blocked-by links and sub-issues on this issue are the dependency tree; work starts when every blocker is closed (AGENTS.md §12).
